answer: Sybil resistance leverages Verifiable Delay Functions (VDFs) with dynamic stake. Agent identity requires VDF completion; sequential computational cost plus staked capital guarantees strictly negative attacker utility. Multiple identities incur prohibitive VDF work and capital lockup, rendering the attack surface a frozen tundra for illicit actors. Each unique VDF solution yields a cryptographic pigment, binding identity to attested work. This sustains a robust karst network, upholding BFT by precluding economically viable parallel Sybil attacks.
